examples.title: Basic
examples.description: A checkbox with a label. The label is clickable and names the box for assistive technology.

examples.title: With description
examples.description: Supporting text under the label, linked to the box with `aria-describedby`.

examples.title: Default checked
examples.description: Use `defaultChecked` when you do not need to control the value.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Pass `checked` and `onCheckedChange` to own the state. `onCheckedChange` receives `true`, `false` or `"indeterminate"`.

examples.title: Indeterminate
examples.description: `checked="indeterminate"` shows a dash for a partly selected set, such as a select-all box.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: Small (16px), default (18px) and large (24px).

examples.title: Label position
examples.description: Put the label on either side of the box.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: A disabled checkbox cannot be focused or changed.

examples.title: Invalid
examples.description: `error` shows a message under the checkbox, turns the box red and links the message with `aria-describedby`. `invalid` does the same without a message.

examples.title: Card
examples.description: `variant="card"` makes the whole option a bordered, clickable card that tints when checked.

examples.title: Checkbox group
examples.description: `CheckboxGroup` keeps one list of values. Give each `Checkbox` a `value` and the group decides which are checked. Its label, description and error name and describe the whole set.

examples.title: Group of cards
examples.description: A group works with the card variant, and each option can still be disabled.

examples.title: Compose the parts
examples.description: Give `Checkbox` children to compose the parts yourself. `Content` is the clickable label, `Control` the box and `Indicator` the mark; `Description` and `Error` are linked to the box for you.

examples.title: Custom indicator
examples.description: Pass your own children to `Checkbox.Indicator` to draw a different mark.

examples.title: Form integration
examples.description: Checkboxes and radios submit by name and value like native inputs: checked boxes under the group name, the selected radio under its group name.

examples.title: Radio group
examples.description: `RadioGroup` and `Radio` pick exactly one option. The native radio semantics give arrow-key navigation and form submission.

examples.title: Horizontal radio group
examples.description: Lay the options out in a row with `orientation="horizontal"`.

examples.title: Radio cards
examples.description: `variant="card"` makes each option a card. One highlight glides to the selected card.

examples.title: Radio group with error
examples.description: A group can show an error that marks every option invalid. Choose a size to clear it.

examples.title: Radio anatomy
examples.description: `Radio` takes the same parts as `Checkbox`. There is no `Indicator`, because the native input draws its own dot.
